Give them a break! Nobody can adjust right away in a situation like this.

Let's find a way to close a plea bargain.
As long as we pay the money, Muranishi will be released.
Scrape together the one hundred million yen bail by next month with everything you have!

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Godan verb.

examples.text: このペンを使ってもいいですか。
もっと英語を使いましょう。

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Very common colloquial pronunciation/variant of すみません.

examples.text: すいません、ちょっと通してください。
examples.trans: Excuse me, please let me through.

meanings.note: In 役に立つ, means 'to be useful / come in handy'.

examples.text: この辞書はとても役に立ちます。
何かお役に立てますか。
examples.trans: Can I be of any help?

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

examples.text: 一円も稼いでねえじゃねえかよ！本気でやってんのかよ！
examples.trans: You haven't earned a single yen! Are you even trying seriously!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Potential stem + そう (稼げそう) means 'looks like one can earn well'.

examples.text: しっかりお金を稼ぎます。
今月はよく稼げました。
examples.trans: I was able to earn well this month.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

examples.text: しかたないだろ！こんな状況ですぐに対応できるはずがない。
examples.trans: Give them a break! Nobody can adjust right away in a situation like this.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。
お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').
Used with が before it (ストーリーが必要だ 'a story is needed') or な before a noun.
分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Ichidan verb.

examples.text: もう少しよく考えてみます。
examples.trans: I'll think about it a little more carefully.

examples.text: 何とか司法取引を成立させよう。
examples.trans: Let's find a way to close a plea bargain.

examples.text: 八十万ドルが支払われました。司法取引の成立です。
examples.trans: Eight hundred thousand dollars was paid. The plea bargain went through.

examples.text: 何とか司法取引を成立させよう。
examples.trans: Let's find a way to close a plea bargain.

examples.text: それでも商売が成立するんでね。
examples.trans: And our business is thriving even without them.

examples.text: 八十万ドルが支払われました。司法取引の成立です。
examples.trans: Eight hundred thousand dollars was paid. The plea bargain went through.

meanings.note: Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

examples.text: 金さえ払えば、村西さんは釈放される。
examples.trans: As long as we pay the money, Muranishi will be released.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: 金さえ払えば、村西さんは釈放される。
examples.trans: As long as we pay the money, Muranishi will be released.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.note: Noun.

examples.text: 来月から新しい仕事が始まる。
examples.trans: My new job starts next month.

examples.text: 来月また会いましょう。

meanings.en: nothing more than (after past verb); up to
meanings.note: After a plain verb + です (出店したまでです), modestly states 'we simply did that and nothing more'.

examples.text: 念のため聞いたまでです。
examples.trans: I merely asked just in case.

examples.text: 来月までに保釈金の一億、死ぬ気で集めてこい！
examples.trans: Scrape together the one hundred million yen bail by next month with everything you have!

examples.text: 金魚が死んでしまった。

examples.trans: I don't want to die yet.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

examples.text: 実際のとこ、どうなんだよ？
examples.trans: In reality, how do things look?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

examples.text: バカかお前、池沢に頼んだらおっさんが納得しねえよ！
examples.trans: Are you crazy, if we begged Ikezawa the boss would never stand for it!

examples.text: だったら俺を納得させる材料を持ってきてくれ。話はそれからだ。
examples.trans: If you want this, bring me proof that convinces me. Then we will talk.

examples.text: ほら貝です。ご納得いただけましたか？
examples.trans: That sound is a conch shell. Have we convinced you?

meanings.note: Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
